sections.title: Batch 6B — header fix, "Install this app", reputation engine v2 (17 Nov 2026)
points: Header (D-059): measured, never cut off: it hides the "Ctrl K" hint, then the name next to the avatar, then moves Sound and language into the account menu (visitors: "More"), then switches to the mobile menu. Every menu stays inside the window (8 px margin); a long email ends with "…". Checked in the browser for every role, English and Urdu, at 10 widths from 360 to 1920 px.

Install this app (D-060): an invitation on the second page (or after 30 s) for everyone, once per 14 days, with 🔊; a permanent "Install this app" button at the bottom of every page. The browser's own question where it exists; otherwise steps with pictures (Chrome/Edge menu, iPhone Safari Share → Add to Home Screen, "open in Safari", "use Chrome or Edge"). No website can install itself: the person always presses "Install".

Reputation engine v2, rep-2 (D-061 to D-066): recency off for reviews; reviews from brand-new customer accounts count, but all together at most one review; many reviews in a few days count half; the platform's typical rating as the starting point; "Best track record" orders by the middle estimate. Chosen and tested with a pre-registered protocol: candidates, rule and success criteria fixed first; selection on the Batch 6 seeds; the choice frozen in a commit; one run on 30 new seeds.

SIMULATION result (test seeds, not a real-world result): S1, S2 and S3 met — as good as the plain Beta without attacks (NDCG@10 0.936), much better under naive fake accounts and collusion (sybil_k10 0.934 against 0.758 for the plain average), better than rep-1 in 97–100% of seeds. rep-2 is live. Not solved: an attacker who first hires other workers (worse than the plain average there); a young platform with mostly first-time customers is slightly below the plain Beta.

What people see: "My reputation" and the Help Centre guide list the live rules from the server (GET /api/meta/reputation-rules); new per-review reasons; the public depth word follows the visible reviews; "Best track record" explains that new workers start in the middle. Urdu "I did come" is gender-neutral.
Texts: new and changed texts in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu (docs/i18n/REVIEW-BATCH-6B.md).

sections.title: Batch 6 — Module 4: bookings, reviews and the reputation engine (16–17 Nov 2026)
points: Work Booking: a customer requests one worker (picture choices for work, day and time; area; description), the worker hears the request (🔊) and accepts or declines; both press "Work done", or one side and 72 hours pass; cancellations with reasons (a worker's late cancellation counts double); "Worker did not come" from the start + 2 hours; one small dispute step decided by an admin (D-039 to D-042, D-049, D-050, D-053, D-054).

Phone numbers (D-002 delivered, D-052): only inside GET /api/bookings/:id, only to the two people and admins, only while accepted and for 7 days after the close; never in lists, the directory, profiles, notifications or CSV files. Free texts are refused when they contain a phone number, email, link or CNIC-like number.

Reviews: after completed work only, once, never edited (1–5 stars, four quick thumbs, would hire again, optional comment with voice typing, read-back before sending); the worker replies once and can report; admins hide with a reason (never for being negative) or restore (D-041, D-051).

Reputation engine: a weighted Beta reputation model (Jøsang & Ismail 2002) with provenance, recency, reviewer-trust and repeat-customer weights; expected value, uncertainty, a cautious lower estimate and a depth word; a reliability record from booking outcomes; a snapshot on the worker profile rebuilt after every change and daily (D-043 to D-048). Pure functions, unit tested with hand-worked examples.

Display: public profile (stars with the count, depth in words, star bars, "x of y" quick answers, reliability counts, reviews with replies, "Done through this platform"), directory and compare lines, "Best track record" sort with an honest note, "Has done jobs on this platform" filter; the worker's "My reputation" page in plain words with 🔊 (D-045, D-047).
Admin: Bookings, Disputes, Reviews and Reputation flags pages, a Reputation tab per worker, Overview charts of bookings and stars, bookings and reviews CSV exports (no phone numbers).
Notifications: 16 new booking and review types; customers get a "Notifications" menu link with the unread count (D-057).

Evaluation by SIMULATION (backend/evaluation/reputation/, 30 seeds, 11 scenarios, four baselines, ablations). Finding: with the provisional parameters the model is not better than the plain average overall, and recent fake reviews still buy places; the individual defences reduce the attacks they target. Parameters were not changed (D-048, D-058). Simulation results only, not real-world results.

sections.title: Batch 5 — Listen, Speak, See: audio help, voice typing and picture choices (14–16 Nov 2026)
points: Listen (🔊): a Listen button under every box of the worker and customer screens says what to do there, and the same help opens in large text. The sound comes from a clip the team recorded, else a voice on the device, else the help is shown on screen with the words "no voice on this device" (D-034). Roman Urdu users hear the Urdu audio.

Speak (🎤): voice typing on names, city, trade, job, search, skills description and numbers (phone digit by digit, years and rupees as amounts; nothing is written when a number is not understood). Never on password, CNIC or email (D-035). A one-time notice explains that the browser sends the voice to its maker's service. After voice typing the website reads back what it wrote, and Undo brings the old text back.

See: picture choices instead of drop-downs for trade (the nine trade drawings), availability, the skill of a proof photo and the proof kind; every picture can be heard; field icons; buttons with an icon and a word.
Page help: a round speaker button in the same corner of every in-scope page, and a Sound menu in the header (show Listen/Speak, read aloud by itself). Settings stay on this device only.
Language chooser: each language card can be heard ("press here for Urdu"), and the one-time question "Should the website read aloud?" follows the choice.
Voice check page (/voice-check, linked from the Help Centre): which voices and clips this device has, test sentences, a microphone test, and how to add an Urdu voice on Android.

Recorded clips: /dev/recorder (development builds only) for the team to record the Urdu help in their own voices; npm run audio:manifest; docs/audio/RECORDING-GUIDE.md. The service worker (v2) keeps clips for offline use; API answers are still never cached. No clips are recorded yet.
Texts: 152 new or changed texts in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu are drafts until the team checks them (docs/i18n/REVIEW-BATCH-5.md, D-031).
